AXIS_OBJECTS.description: Where published artifacts and the generated indexes are stored. This is the repository: losing the bucket loses everything served from it.

AXIS_ADMIN_USERNAME.description: Username for the first admin account, created on first run. Nothing else creates an account, so a deployment without this has no way in. Once that account exists this is no longer read, and can be dropped from `vars` at your convenience — renaming it here does not rename the account.

AXIS_ADMIN_PASSWORD.description: Password for that first account, at least 8 characters. A shorter one fails the first sign-in rather than seeding an account nobody can use. Delete it once you have signed in: it is not read again, and until it is gone the account's original password is sitting in the deployment. Set `AXIS_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH` instead to avoid handing over a plaintext password at all.

UPLOAD_BACKEND.description: How artifact bytes reach the bucket. `r2`, the default, hands publishing clients a presigned URL so the bytes go straight to R2 — this needs the three R2 credentials below, and a deployment that leaves them blank fails at sign-in rather than at the first publish. `local-r2` sends the bytes through the Worker instead: nothing else to supply, but billed for the whole transfer and capped by the Worker's memory.

AXIS_SESSION_SECRET.description: Signs admin session cookies. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`. Changing it signs everyone out; unlike the bootstrap password it is needed for as long as the deployment runs.

TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER.description: Salts publish token hashes, so a copy of the stored hashes cannot be cracked offline. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`. Changing it invalidates every publish token already issued — CI using one stops being able to publish.

SIGNING_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET.description: Encrypts repository signing keys before they are stored, so the keys apt clients trust are never at rest in the clear. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`. Lose it and the stored keys cannot be read back, which means re-signing every repository under a new key that clients have to be told about.

R2_BUCKET_NAME.description: The bucket this Worker is deployed with, named again here because signed URLs address it by name and a binding does not report the bucket it points at. If you renamed the bucket while setting this up, use that name: a mismatch leaves reads working through the binding while every upload and download addresses a bucket that is not yours.

R2_ACCOUNT_ID.description: Your Cloudflare account ID, which is the host presigned upload URLs are signed for. Found on the right of the dashboard overview, or in the URL after `dash.cloudflare.com/`.

R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID.description: Access key ID of an R2 API token with object read and write on this Worker's bucket. Create one under [R2 > Manage API tokens](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/r2/api-tokens). This is not the same thing as the bucket binding: the binding is how the Worker reads objects, this is what lets it hand a client a URL to write one.

R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.description: Secret access key of that same R2 API token, shown once when the token is created. Without it, the access key ID, and the account ID, artifact uploads are refused: every request is answered by a single Durable Object, so a Worker that cannot sign upload URLs fails at sign-in rather than at the first publish. Set `UPLOAD_BACKEND=local-r2` to run without any of them.

scripts.build: pnpm --filter @axis-repository/core build && pnpm --filter @axis-repository/admin-ui build && pnpm --filter @axis-repository/publish-client build && pnpm --filter @axis-repository/runtime-cloudflare build:worker
scripts.verify: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build && pnpm check:boundaries && pnpm coverage && pnpm check:audit && pnpm deploy:dry-run:worker && pnpm check:release-docs
